title: HostDesiredState
description:
What one host should be running. The daemon watches this document at the path its
`paths.desired_state_file` names and converges on every change to it.

httpCache.description: Absent, the response cache names itself `nibrunner` and no purge is served.

maxApps.description:
How many apps this host is to hold a slot for, when that is more than `max_apps` in its
config.toml: the running daemon widens to it in place, with no restart. It never narrows
the host below its configuration, and absent, the configuration alone says.

revision.description:
What whoever wrote this document calls this version of it, carried back in the report as
`acceptedRevision`. Nothing on the host reads it: it is not ordered and not checked
against the one before it, so a document may name any version it likes. Required, so that
a control plane can always ask which of its own versions a host is on — and so a host
answering with one nobody wrote is impossible.

cutoverTimeoutMs.description:
How long a new `deploymentId` is given to become healthy beside the deployment it
replaces, running or asleep, before its hostnames are moved over to it and the old one is
stopped (and its snapshot deleted). A new deployment that is not healthy by then is stopped
and the old one keeps its hostnames, serving or woken on request. Absent, the old
deployment is stopped before the new one starts. An instance with a volume is always
replaced that way, since two guests cannot write one disk.

firstBoot.description: Whether the host boots the instance once it is declared, or leaves it to its first request.

snapshotTtlMs.description:
How long the memory snapshot of an instance asleep is kept without a wake. Past that it is
deleted, and the next request boots the instance afresh. Absent, it is kept until the next
wake. Only an instance that sleeps has a snapshot for this to apply to.

httpPort.description:
The guest port the HTTP proxy sends this app's hostnames to, and the one the health check
probes.

ports.description: What this app answers on besides `httpPort`, if anything.

CacheName.description: a lowercase letter, then at most 31 lowercase letters, digits or `-`

CachePeer.description: an https URL naming an IP address and optionally a port, without a path

CachePurge.description:
Where an app purges what the response cache holds of it, and the hosts a purge reaches.

`POST https://<hostname><path>` with `authorization: Bearer v1.<owner>.<signature>`, the
signature `HMAC-SHA256(key, "mf-cache-purge\0" || owner)` in unpadded base64url under any of
`keys`, and `{"tags": [...]}`, removes every stored answer of `owner` carrying one of the tags:
here, then on every peer. `owner` is the `app` label of the instances it covers, or the app id
of one without that label.

keys.description: Two while the key is being rotated, so a token signed under either is taken.

peers.description: Every other host, each asked to purge too before the purge is answered.

Command.description:
What the guest runs once its root is stacked, as uid 65534: `program` with `args`, in
`workingDirectory`, with `environment`. The working directory is made if it is not there,
given to that uid, and is where the program's persistent state lives, because everything
under the root persists on the volume and nowhere else is the program's to write.

DesiredHttpCache.description:
How the response cache of `[proxy.http.cache]` is shared: what it calls itself to visitors, and
how an app purges it across every host.

activation.description:
What puts this instance to sleep and what tells the host it is ready. A `sleepWhen` other
than `never` is refused on anything but an `on-request` instance. A change under the same
`deploymentId` restarts nothing: the next idle evaluation reads the new `sleepWhen`, a
frozen guest that may no longer sleep on traffic is thawed, the next pass applies
`snapshotTtlMs`, and `cutoverTimeoutMs` is the next cut-over's (one under way keeps its
deadline). `firstBoot` only says how an instance this host has not booted yet comes up.

deploymentId.description:
A running instance is replaced when this changes, and only then: a new layer or config
under the same `deploymentId` is not picked up. `activation`, `expiry`, `limits`,
`labels`, `hostnames` and `desiredState` are taken up in place.

expiry.description:
Optional terminal retention for on-request instances: expired hostnames answer HTTP 410.
Removing the policy or changing deploymentId revives the instance. A changed `idleMs` or
`deadline` under the same `deploymentId` is read by the next expiry check, measured from
the instant the policy was first named; it never revives an instance already expired.

hostnames.description:
What the HTTP proxy routes to this app's `httpPort`. Empty for an app nothing outside needs
to reach by name.

idleTimeoutMs.description:
How long an `on-request` instance stays up after its last request before it sleeps: the
older spelling of `activation.sleepWhen`, refused beside it. 300000 when neither is named.

labels.description:
What the control plane calls this instance: at most 8 opaque pairs, echoed in the report
and on every log line and request record it writes. Taken up without replacing the
deployment.

layers.description: The root filesystem, bottom layer first. At least one; at most `MAX_LAYERS`.

limits.description: What the host enforces beyond `config.resources`, applied without a new deployment.

scratch.description: What the instance writes to when it has no volume.

volumeId.description:
One of this document's `volumes`, stacked writable over the layers. Absent when `scratch`
is named instead; one of the two always is.

DesiredInstanceState.description: The whole of an instance's activation policy.

oneOf.description:
Brings the microVM up for the first deploy (unless `activation.firstBoot` is `lazy`, when the
first request does) and for every request that finds it asleep, and
lets it sleep again once it has been quiet for `idleTimeoutMs`.
Takes the microVM down and leaves the app reachable enough to say so.

DesiredLayer.description:
One read-only layer of the root filesystem an instance boots into. Layers stack in the order
the document lists them, first at the bottom, and the app's volume — or its scratch — is
stacked writable over all of them. The kind says what the object is, and so what the host does with it.

oneOf.description:
An OCI image for Linux x86_64, from an artifact-store archive or public registry. Its image
configuration does not replace the instance's explicit command or guest account.
A squashfs or ext4 image, attached as it was uploaded.

objectKey.description: Where the object lives in the store.

oneOf.description:
One program, packed into an image at `destinationPath` and run the way this host has
always run one: by the guest's own init, with the app's arguments and environment.

objectKey.description: Where the object lives in the store.

oneOf.description:
One program the host fetches for itself from `url`, so that nothing has to be put in the
store first. `digest` is the program's: of the response, or of `zipEntry` inside it when the
URL serves a zip, or of `tarEntry` inside it when the URL serves a `.tar.xz`. Nothing is
made from the bytes before they match it. At most one of the two entries is named.

initialContents.description: Absent for a volume that starts empty.

DownloadUrl.description: an https URL of at most 2048 characters

ExecutablePath.description: an absolute path to a file other than /sbin/init

deadline.description: Stop new requests at this instant, then expire after admitted requests finish.

FirstBoot.description:
When an `on-request` instance is first booted. `lazy` leaves it as one asleep with nothing to
wake from: its hostnames answer, but neither its layers nor any memory are held for it until a
request fetches and boots it. Refused on anything but an `on-request` instance, which nothing would wake.

HealthCheck.description:
What tells this host an instance is well — and so what a wake waits for before it hands the
caller on, and what the instance's liveness is read from after that. Named in every document:
a default would be a kind nobody chose, and the one that looks obvious lies. A TCP connect is
answered by the guest kernel's accept queue whether or not the process behind it will ever
read the request, so a program that has stopped answering passes it for as long as it lives.

oneOf.description: A connection to `httpPort` is accepted. Only that — for a port that does not speak HTTP.

The microVM is up and `httpPort` has accepted a connection once: the tenant is listening.
That is all it is asked, and only until it answers — a guest this host did not build
answers no path it was not told about — so its liveness after that is the microVM being up.

InitialContents.description:
What a volume holds before its app has written a byte: an archive in the store — a tar,
gzipped or not, or a zip — unpacked under `destinationPath` in the app's root as the volume is
formatted. That happens once, so this is read once: a volume already formatted is its app's,
and a change here does nothing to it.

destinationPath.description:
The directory the archive's entries land under, as the app sees it. Made if no layer holds
it, and given — with everything unpacked into it — to the uid the program runs as.

objectKey.description: Where the object lives in the store.

InstanceLabels.description: At most 8 opaque labels, echoed in the report and on every log line and request record.

InstanceLimits.description:
What the host enforces on an instance beyond what `resources` gives it. Every field is optional
and applied live, without replacing the deployment: a running microVM's cgroup is rewritten and
the proxy's limit takes the next request.

concurrent.description:
Requests the proxy carries to this instance at once, in place of the host's
`proxy.http.concurrency.app_concurrent`. Its host-wide limit still applies.

cpuPercent.description:
Host CPU time in percent of one core, enforced as a `cpu.max` quota that only ever tightens
the `vcpuCount` cores `resources` gives: `25` is a quarter of a core, and a value above
`vcpuCount × 100` changes nothing.

InstancePort.description:
A port a guest answers on beside its HTTP one, carried to it unread.

It carries whatever arrives, tcp or udp: a port is a port, the relay in front of a host
forwards both for every one in its range, and a guest that listens on only one of them
answers the other with a port-unreachable the way any host would.

memoryMib.description:
A multiple of 2: guest memory is backed by transparent huge pages, which Firecracker
requires in 2 MiB multiples.

LabelKey.description: a lowercase letter, then at most 31 lowercase letters, digits, `_` or `-`

LabelValue.description: 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits or any of `._:/@+-`

MemoryPolicy.description:
How the kernel treats this instance's memory when the host runs short. None of it changes the
guest's RAM or the cgroup's hard ceiling, which `resources` decides.

swapMib.description: Maximum uncompressed bytes allowed in host swap, in MiB. Zero disables swap.

targetMib.description: Working-set target, capped by the hard memory budget. Does not resize guest RAM.

MemoryPriority.description:
`production` keeps its target resident (`memory.low`) and is the last the OOM killer picks;
`preview` and `build` are throttled at their target (`memory.high`) and picked first.

OciRepository.description: a lowercase registry hostname and repository path, without a scheme, tag or digest

PortName.description: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter

PurgePath.description: an absolute path of at most 256 printable characters, without a query or fragment

Revision.description: between 1 and 128 printable characters, without spaces

Scratch.description:
A writable root that lives and dies with the microVM, in place of a volume: it starts empty at
every cold boot, is kept through a sleep because the snapshot keeps what the guest held, and is
gone once the instance is stopped, replaced or expired. It is never a volume: never reported,
never checkpointed, never exported.

oneOf.description:
A tmpfs in the guest's own memory, so what is written to it is paid for out of
`config.resources.memoryMib`.

A sparse ext4 file the host makes at every cold boot and deletes once the microVM is gone,
so what is written to it costs the host's disk rather than the guest's memory.

SleepPolicy.description:
What puts a running microVM back to sleep. Only an `on-request` instance may carry one that
fires: nothing else on this host would wake it again, and the next reconcile pass would bring
it straight back up.

StoredObject.description:
An object in the store the host's `artifacts.store_url` names, checked against `digest`
before anything is made from it. The digest is the whole of what is checked: a `sizeBytes`
beside it, which a document used to carry, is read past.

objectKey.description: Where the object lives in the store.

TarEntry.description: a relative path of between 1 and 512 characters

TenantArguments.description: The arguments the binary is started with.

TenantValue.description: Only complete `${NAME}` references are filled in for NAME in NIBRUN_HOSTNAME, NIBRUN_HTTP_PORT. Bare names, incomplete references and other dollar signs remain literal; complete references to unknown `NIBRUN_` names are refused.

Timestamp.description: an ISO 8601 instant with an offset

ZipEntry.description: a relative path of between 1 and 512 characters
